Project 3-1
Project plan template
Preamble
Every researcher but also heads of R&D, marketing groups, and companies have to write research and development plans. Sometimes different names like market analysis or business plan are used in business environments. However, the key structure and purpose of all of these documents is very similar: to convince someone to invest into your ideas. 
Here we provide you with a template for writing professional project plans. The template is strongly inspired by the H2020 template used for proposing European Research projects.
Work like a professional scientist
Given that you are writing a project plan for a research project it is key that you argue your ideas and approach properly based on scientific literature and state-of-the-art related work. Do not make claims you cannot support with scientific literature or own scientific results. Avoid speculations. But if you must, clearly say when you speculate. Working as a professional scientist means that you take responsibility for your actions and the results of your research. So you must analyse your own work critically. Critical analysis means self-reflection and a clear statement of the (potential) impact of your work (advantages and disadvantages).
Plagiarism will not be tolerated
Plagiarism in your research plan will not be tolerated. Keep in mind: Plagiarism is not just copying text and images. Plagiarism is also stealing ideas or pretending that you are the first having such an idea. You cannot protect yourself by claiming lack of knowledge. As a scientist it is your job to ensure that you studied the field or research sufficiently so that you know relevant related work! 
Dividing and taking responsibility
In you project group make sure that everyone contributes to the project plan. Take responsibility, divide work, but also support each other. For each section you are asked to name responsible authors and colleagues who act as internal reviewers. Every section should be checked by at least one person in addition to the original author. It is not accepted that you write: we all did everything.: Make sure to properly distribute the writing work (about) equally. Everyone must contribute.
Shared documents 
While we prefer Latex for writing professional publications even under exact scientists it is common to write project plans together by using shared Word files. You can e.g. copy the template to Google docs to work together efficiently on the document at the same time.

1 Excellence
1.1 Motivation, context, problem statement
Provide a concise description of: What is the exact problem you try to solve? Why is it important to solve this problem? Provide the necessary context (e.g. why is your customer). Support your claims with references! Provide precise numbers. (1 page max)
Example:
The world's population aged 65 and over continues growing. Today, 8.5 percent of people worldwide (617 million) are aged 65 and over (UN). The number of older persons aged 60 years and over is expected to more than double by 2050 and to more than triple by 2100, rising from 962 million globally in 2017 to 2.1 billion in 2050 and 3.1 billion in 2100 (NIH). The global population of people aged 80 and older is expected to more than triple between 2015 and 2050, growing from 126.5 million to 446.6 million (UN). 
This development generates increasing pressure on health-care systems worldwide and generates a demand for new technologies supporting elderly care. Maintaining the independence of elderly for as long as possible represents one way to unload the health-care systems in general and caregivers in particular. More importantly, relative independence also increases the quality of life of elderly (Galik, Resnick, and Pretzer-Aboff 2009). Stähelin (Stahelin 2000) characterizes the positive relation between functioning, physical activity, and mobility on an older person’s independence. Verdote-Robertson and Reddon (Verdote-Robertson and Reddon 2000) too signal how older persons’ level of mobility benefits their self-efficacy. Research also shows a positive correlation between physical activity and their effect on various moods, such as depression (Williams and Tappen 2007, Williams and Tappen 2008). Studies also suggest how physical activity, or individualized activities, can improve elderly’s sleep patterns (Richards et al. 2005). 
Serious games are one approach to increase the level of physical activity, for balance and muscle strength training in elderly. Serious games consists of two core components, namely the element of learning and the element of assessment (Michael and Chen 2005). Elderly benefit from the game element: Research shows that the use of serious games helps to obtain a longer cooperation of the players due to the entertaining environment and thus to more motivation to continue the training (Bortoli and Gaggi 2011). Studies also look at employing affection in serious games for improving the well-being of the elderly (Styliadis et al. 2014).  
In this project we develop a novel game device that helps elderly to stay fit. The game device is being developed in cooperation with our customer, the Maastricht elderly care center. The project puts special emphasis to develop the game device and human-machine interfaces in such a way that elderly can operate the game device without help from caregivers. This is to avoid adding to the already high workload of caregivers. We will evaluate if these goals have been successfully achieved through a user study with 50 elderly participants.

1.2 Scientific and technological objectives
Formulate Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Timely (SMART) Objectives. Number objectives so that these get clear identifiers (O1, O2, …). Formulate Key Performance Indicators for each objective that make the success of these objectives measurable. Link objectives to tasks in your work plan so that reviewers know where you are actually addressing these objectives. Objectives can be technological objectives that enhance products and services as well as scientific objectives that aim at generating new insights (knowledge). Given that you are conducting science there must be scientific objectives. Scientific objectives must be formulated precisely in form of research questions. (2 pages max.)
EDUROB (project name) will tackle challenges in the areas of Educational Robotics, Psychometrics, Healthcare, Human-Machine Interaction, and Artificial Intelligence, while paying particular attention to ethical and legal issues that may arise from the use of robotics and AI in education for primary school aged children in school. To achieve the EDUROB vision, the main goals of EDUROB have been broken down into several Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Timely (SMART) Objectives (O) that mutually benefit each other. Concrete KPIs have been defined for each objective to measure REAS success.
Objective O1: Delivery of social robot that stimulates learning of children.
Objective O1: Delivery of social robot that stimulates learning of children.
Addressed in Task 1 and 2
S.M.A.R.T. Justification
The central goal of EDUROB is to develop a social robot that stimulates learning of children in the educational environments. This robot observes children during educational task and assesses the children’s mood and engagement through classification of body posture and facial expressions. The robot then encourages the child if it gets bored or sleepy.

1.3 Requirements
Describe requirements that you identified during your discussion with your customers and requirements you found during your initial research. Such requirements can include user interfaces and usability, hardware requirements, software requirements, privacy-related requirements, … . Number requirements to provide them with a unique identifier. Group requirements properly into categories. Provide clearly defined priorities for requirements (e.g. priority 1 means “not negotiable, if not fulfilled, project is considered a fail”, priority 3 means “will be done if time permits, nice to have”). (2 pages max)
R1 Programming languages
R1.1 Algorithms should be implemented in C++. (priority 1)
R1.2 The User Interfaces (UI) should be implemented in Python. (priority 2)
R2 System architecture
R2.1. The harbor simulator should be implemented in form of independently functioning programs that communicate through a set of shared files (repository architecture). (priority 1)
R2.2. Individual software programs include: (1) a user interface that visualizes the movement of ships, (2) a simulator that allows the simulation of a harbor model, (3) a model editor that allows to edit the structure of the harbor model from a graphical user interface, (4) an optimization tool that allows finding best control parameters for the harbor model. (priority 1)
R2.2. A common user interface should be provided that allows access to the individual software programs. (priority 3)

Describe your chosen approach. Argue properly based on scientific literature and state-of-the-art, why your chosen approaches are feasible. Provide a proper overview before going into details. The approach should e.g. properly explain: which algorithms you choose for which reason, involved/required datasets, user studies/validation procedures, software development approach, system overview, required hardware. Where possible provide a better overview with the help of graphics (e.g. a diagram to show the system architecture). After reading this section customers and examiners should understand what you will be doing, that the intended work meets objectives and requirements, and should be confident that you can actually do the work that you promise. For this provide references to approaches you are reusing or adapting (e.g. existing software tools, algorithms, datasets). You do not have to develop everything from scratch. Instead concentrate on the interesting aspects of your work. (3 pages max)
